title: Prime-to-characteristic finite-coefficient acyclicity of geometric affine space
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. For $r\geq0$ let $V=\mathbf A^r_k$ [def-sbc-affine-space]. Use ordinary small-etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and the roots-of-unity twists $\Lambda(t)$ for $t\in\mathbf Z$ [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Pullback of constant sections induces an isomorphism
$$\Lambda(t)(k)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^0(V,\Lambda(t)),$$
and $H^q(V,\Lambda(t))=0$ for every integer $q\ne0$. Here $\Lambda(t)(k)$ is the rank-one $\Lambda$-module of sections on $\operatorname{Spec}k$; no choice of primitive root is part of the isomorphism. The assertion includes $r=0$, characteristic zero, and fields of arbitrary transcendence degree.

source.place: Section 16, Example 16.3, affine-line Kummer calculation and affine-space acyclicity via Section 22; Section 16 opening paragraphs on trivializing twists over an algebraically closed field

proof.text: Put $m=\ell^n$. Choose a primitive $m$-th root $\zeta\in k$ by [lem-sc-primitive-root]. For every $k$-scheme $T$, the map $a\mapsto\zeta^a$ identifies $\Lambda_T$ with $\mu_{m,T}$. Indeed $z^m-1=\prod_{a\in\mathbf Z/m}(z-\zeta^a)$ has pairwise unit differences, so a root on any etale object is uniquely a choice of one $\zeta^a$ on a clopen partition; this is exactly a locally constant $\mathbf Z/m$-valued section. This description commutes with restriction and every $k$-pullback. The signed tensor powers and duals defining the twists in [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] consequently give compatible trivializations $\Lambda_T\cong\Lambda_T(t)$ for every integer $t$. Negative powers use the basis dual to the chosen tensor basis. Only the computation uses this auxiliary basis.

source.place: Section 16 opening paragraphs, p.107: twists and primitive-root trivialization

proof.text: For every sheaf occurring here, $H^q=0$ for $q<0$: in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] its injective resolution starts in degree zero. We may compute the underlying abelian-sheaf cohomology or fixed-$\Lambda$ module cohomology interchangeably. To justify this precisely, apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-derived-direct-image-comparison] to the structure map to $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-algebraically-closed-etale-sheaf-constant], sheaves on $s$ are naturally their section sets with constant-sheaf realization. Transporting addition and scalar multiplication gives the analogous equivalence for module sheaves; applying the equivalence termwise identifies derived direct image to $s$ with module-valued derived global sections. The stated comparison is therefore the required cohomology comparison and respects constants. For $r=0$, [def-sbc-affine-space] gives $\mathbf A^0_k=s$. The finite twist is a torsion sheaf, and [lem-sf-separably-closed-torsion-cd] gives $H^q(s,\Lambda(t))=0$ for $q>0$. Degree zero is its sections $\Lambda(t)(k)$, and the constants map is the identity.

source.place: Tag 03QQ, section-cohomology-point, lemma-equivalence-abelian-sheaves-point and lemma-compare-cohomology-point; nonnegative resolutions

proof.text: Apply [thm-pur-kummer-affine-line] with $N=n$, $R=\Lambda$ and the finite free rank-one $R$-module $A=\Lambda$. Clause (1) gives $H^q(\mathbf A^1_k,\Lambda(1))=0$ for $q>0$ and a degree-zero isomorphism from $\Lambda$ sending $a$ to the section $\zeta\otimes a$. Under Step 1 this is exactly the constants map for $\Lambda$. Thus the canonical constants map $u_1:\Lambda[0]\to R\Gamma(\mathbf A^1_k,\Lambda)$ is an isomorphism: it induces an isomorphism on degree zero and on every other degree (both groups being zero, including negative degrees by Step 2); apply [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology]. Step 2 supplies the fixed-module interpretation needed here.

source.place: Section 16, Example 16.3, p.109: affine-line Kummer calculation

proof.text:
For $j\geq0$ let $u_j:\Lambda[0]\to R\Gamma(\mathbf A^j_k,\Lambda)$ be the canonical constants map. Step 2 gives $u_0$ invertible and Step 3 gives $u_1$ invertible. Suppose $u_j$ is invertible. The affine polynomial description in [def-sbc-affine-space] identifies $\mathbf A^j_k\times_k\mathbf A^1_k$ with $\mathbf A^{j+1}_k$: $k[x_1,\ldots,x_j]\otimes_k k[y]=k[x_1,\ldots,x_j,y]$ via the mutually inverse maps on the displayed generators. Both factors are finite type since these polynomial algebras have finitely many generators. Apply [thm-kun-0f1p] with integer coefficient modulus $m=\ell^n$ and both input sheaves $\Lambda$. Its hypotheses hold because $k$ is algebraically closed, hence separably closed, and $m$ is invertible in $k$. By [lem-kun-pullback-constant] and [lem-kun-tensor-unit] the external coefficient is the constant $\Lambda$. We obtain an isomorphism
$$R\Gamma(\mathbf A^j_k,\Lambda)\otimes^L_\Lambda R\Gamma(\mathbf A^1_k,\Lambda)\xrightarrow{\kappa}R\Gamma(\mathbf A^{j+1}_k,\Lambda).$$
The derived tensor functor [def-kun-derived-tensor] sends the two isomorphisms $u_j,u_1$ to an isomorphism. Its source is $\Lambda[0]\otimes^L_\Lambda\Lambda[0]\cong\Lambda[0]$ by the tensor-unit statement at $s$, using the module equivalence in Step 2. Hence the composite $v_{j+1}=\kappa\circ(u_j\otimes^Lu_1)$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 0F1P, lemma-kunneth; Milne Section 16 Example 16.3 and Section 22 Remark 22.3(b)

proof.text: The composite $v_{j+1}$ of Step 4 is $u_{j+1}$. In the formula of [def-kun-kunneth-map], $\kappa$ is adjoint to the two pulled-back counits followed by the coefficient tensor multiplication. Composing with $u_j\otimes^Lu_1$, its adjoint sends $a\otimes b$ to the constant section $ab$: on each factor the counit applied to a pulled-back constant is that constant, by the adjunction triangle identity. The inverse-image composition comparisons in that definition identify this with the adjoint of $u_{j+1}$. Equivalently the two maps agree on $H^0$, sending $1$ to the constant section $1$; a map from the free module $\Lambda[0]$ into a derived module complex is determined by its $H^0$ class, since the complex of maps from $\Lambda$ is the complex itself. This verifies the claimed equality and closes the induction for the specified constants maps. Their targets therefore have only degree-zero cohomology. Finally apply the compatible sheaf trivializations of Step 1. The pullback compatibility in [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] makes the square with $u_j$ and the actual constants map $\Lambda(t)(k)\to H^0(\mathbf A^j_k,\Lambda(t))$ commute. Its two vertical basis maps and top map are isomorphisms, so the bottom map is an isomorphism. Higher and negative vanishing transport through the same sheaf isomorphisms. Changing $\zeta$ changes only the vertical maps; the bottom map is always pullback and is independent of any choice.

source.place: Section 16 opening paragraphs and Example 16.3; Section 22 exterior-product map and its adjunction formula
